F.A. AHMED COLLEGE, GAROIMAI | PROSPECTUS 2026-27
                                                                                       From the Desk of the Principal

F.A. Ahmed College, Garoimari, was established in the year 1984 in the name of Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, the 5th
President of India. At the outset, I would like to express my gratitude to those great personalities who, at the cost of
their selfless efforts, gifted F.A. Ahmed College with the light of higher education, enriching the area. We are elated
                                                 to welcome the new batches of students to the 2026-27 academic
                                                 year of our College. While completing forty-two years of our glorious
                                                 existence, our F. A. Ahmed College assures that it will do its best to
                                                 enrich every newcomer to the College – academically, intellectually,
                                                 and culturally. Our academic staff, non-teaching staff, Governing
                                                 body, Guardians, and well-wishers have always given their best
                                                 endeavors to enhance the institution's immutable glory. With their
                                                 combined support, we aspire to reach the zenith of excellence.

                                                        I am privileged to offer my services as a teacher rather than in
                                               any other profession. Education is part and parcel of changing
                                               people's mindsets. The aims of education should not be confined to
the 3Rs alone, but rather be far beyond this periphery. The primary objective of higher education is to broaden the
thinking of democratic people, which is a very essential skill in the AI world. Our education should enable us to
create a manpower of international standards. The global higher education landscape is becoming increasingly
competitive, making it a much more challenging environment for anyone else. Students are expected to be
Democratic, Liberal, Networking, and Technical to the best of their capacity to overcome such challenges. Apart from
molding an advanced academic career, keeping up with the rest of the world is equally necessary. The time has come
to think about “Quality” rather than “Quantity”. No compromise should be made on the quality of education. Quality
should be ensured, even at the cost of quantity, to realize global excellence.

         Although the Principal is the administrative head of an institution, without the co-operation of staff, it would
be like a pendulum. So, the enhancement of quality education in college is a matter of more priority than any other
matter. I need the cordial cooperation of the college's staff in all spheres. Therefore, my earnest request to all
guardians and residents of the locality is to consider the college their own and use its property to meet collective
needs.




                                                                                    Abdul Awal Sahab
                                                                                      Principal i/c
                                                                             F.A. Ahmed College, Garoimari.
                                     Warm greetings to our aspiring students

I welcome you all and sincerely wish that your promising desire to study and learn at our institute is fulfilled very
soon. Dear aspirants, we are a 42-year-old established institute with a sprawling campus of 25 Bighas and 902
students from nearby districts. Our jewel alums are all over Assam with heads held high wherever they are. Now, as
you plan your future take-offs, life from our institute and be part of our new batch of students, I am very positive

also believe you will enjoy and learn more about life and the institute through our vibrant environment.
         I once again welcome you all to our College, and we promise to bring out your real personality.

                                    Profile of F. A. Ahmed College, Garoimari

The year 1984 of the last century was eventful and epochal in the history of Garoimari and its neighboring areas. At
that time, a handful of people got knowledge literacy; the logic of higher education, by and large, disappeared in the
area. It was almost beyond the dream of producing highly educated people from a manpower-producing industry
established in Garoimari. A few among them realized the need for higher education. Among them, we must include
the following personalities: Omor Ali Sarkar (the founder-president of the Managing Committee), Abdul Hakim (the
Founder-Secretary), and many others who endeavored to establish the college. Abdul Qayyum Al Aman took on the
pioneering role as Honorary Principal of the College when regular classes began. He played an active, pioneering role
in shaping the foundation of the College. Besides, the contributions of all the MLAs of Chhaygaon Constituency since
1980 till date are no less memorable for their all kind of assistance. The minority Muslims people mostly dominate
Garoimari, dependent basically on the agrarian economy. The people of the area spontaneously supported
establishing a college. The mission of the college was to spread the rays of higher education, breaking the barrier of
darkness among rural people.
         In 1984, on an auspicious day, the dream became a reality with the establishment of the higher educational
institution, F.A. Ahmed College. The College is named in memory of Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, an Assamese son who
served as the President of India from 1974 to 1977. It is the only higher educational institution that has been
imparting education in the Degree Classes (Arts) since its inception.
         At the initial stage, Abdur Rahman Khan served as the college's honorary principal. Mr. Habibur Rahman
served as the college's Principal until his retirement on 31st December 2014. The college was provincialized by the
State Government of Assam w.e.f. 01/01/2013, but the Post of the principal was not provincialized. It will always
remain incomparable to him who offers about 24 years of prolonged service. After his departure, Abdul Awal Sahab
has taken charge of the principal and is continuing. The college has a vast, sprawling campus covering 3.34 hectares
(25 bighas) of land, and its serene atmosphere attracts one and all. The co-educational Arts Degree College had a
humble beginning with 161 students and 10 faculty members at its establishment. At present, about 902 students
have been enrolled and facilitated for higher education. The teaching component comprises 30 faculties and various
supporting services, including an ‘Internal Quality Assurance Cell’ (IQAC). The student feedback system has been
introduced to address deficiencies in the course and enhance teaching quality. The college has traversed a long
distance since its inception. It has produced a large number of brilliant students who have been recruited in Govt.
and semi-Govt. Institutions and entered a University, and many of them are well placed in both their social and
personal lives.

Education Poloicy-2020. The medium of instruction is in both Assamese and English.

                                                COMMON COURSES
   Multi-Disciplinary Courses: These are 3-credit courses spanning over five different groups of subjects- (i) Natural
    and Physical Science, (ii) Mathematics, Statistics, and Computer Applications, (iii) Library, Information, and
    Media Sciences, (iv) Commerce and Management, and (v) Humanities and Social Sciences. The level of these
    courses is Class XII.

                                                                                                             Page | 8
    Ability Enhancement Courses (AEC): This is an 8-credit course covering Modern Indian Languages (MIL) and
    English Communication.
   Skill Enhancement Courses (SEC): These are various skill courses with a total credit allocation of 9. In our
    structure, we shall have four skill courses starting from Semester III.
   Value-Based Courses (VAC): The VAC courses will come from four subgroups- (i) Disaster Management, (ii)
    United Nations and Human Rights (iii) Understanding India, (iv) Environmental Science, (v) Digital and
    Technological Solutions, (vi) Health & Wellness, Yoga Education, Sports, and Fitness. Altogether they will have a
    credit allocation of 6.
   Internship: All students of B.A 4th Semester are to carry out an internship with a credit allocation of 4.
As shown in the figures, the base credit score for a 3-Year course is 120 and a student needs to have at least 50% of
120 i.e. 60 credits in a subject to qualify for a major in that subject. In the same way a minor course will have 12
credits and a student can have two minors with a total of 24 credits. Apart from the Major subject, if a student can
obtain 48 credits in a particular subject, the student will get a double major.

Krishna Kanta Handiqui State Open University Study Centre of F. A. Ahmed College, Garoimari was founded in the
year 2007. Initially it was started with Bachelor Preparatory Programme (Now discontinued by university) and
Bachelor Degree programme. Gradually the Centre started offering Master programmes also. As per guide line of the
university the study Centre organizes counseling sessions for the learners on Sundays, Self-Learning Materials (SLM)
are supplied by the university and are distributed by the study Centre.

At present, the study Centre is offering the following Courses
B. A. Honors & Regular Courses in all subjects (Arts Stream).
M.A. Courses in Assamese, Economics, Education, Hindi, Mathematics and Political Science. .
At present, the study center has been imparting education about 350 learners.

General Admission Rules:

Eligibility:
Degree Course: A candidate must pass the Assam State School Education Board ASSEB or equivalent
(10+2 Standard) examination recognized by Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE).
Admission will be based on merit and a personal interview. The prospectus and application form can also be
downloaded from the college website wwe.faac.org.in. Reservations for SC/ST/OBC/MOBC candidates, physically
handicapped candidates, and candidates with proficiency in extracurricular activities will be made as per the
government. Rules and regulations. Complete the application form in all respects and submit it online on or before
the last date of submission. Necessary documents must be uploaded online. The college will not entertain
application for admission received after the last date of submission.

                                               Admission Procedure

i.      Application for Admission to the college should be made in the online application forms available on the
        College website
ii.     Admission is strictly on merit and is governed by the College's admission rules. The Admission Committee's
        decision in this regard is final.
iii.    Applicants will have to appear in person at the time of admission with original copies of the Pass Certificate,
        Mark Sheet, Age Certificate, Character Certificate (from the Heads of the institution last attended), Caste
        Certificate (where necessary), and any other document notified from time to time.
iv.     No applications will be accepted after the submission deadline.
v.      Reservation of seats will be entertained as per the Government rules.
vi.     Extra-Curricular (EC) quota will be maintained as per the Govt. norms in all classes

Fee Structure: The fee structure for different courses will be in accordance with the guidelines of the Government of
Assam. These structures will be notified on the college notice board and the college website.

College Discipline-General Regulations

1. Students must come to the College invariably in the prescribed uniform. They must bring an Identity Card and a
Student's Handbook and produce them when asked for. This rule is considered the minimum requirement for
maintaining the College's discipline.

2. All the students should read the Notice Board of the College regularly and note their own important instructions in
the Student’s Handbook.

3. Students should be decent, courteous, and polite at all times, whether they are in class or on the college premises.

4. Students should respect the beauty and cleanliness of the College and take utmost care to promote the same.

5. Scribbling on books, desks and walls is strictly prohibited and liable to fines.

6. Spitting, writing and sticking anything on the College walls/rooms are strictly prohibited.

7. Students should park their vehicles in the area allotted for the purpose,

8. Disobedience and misbehavior towards staff members or repeated breaking of college rules or behavior
objectionable to the good tone of the school, even outside the college premises will deserve severe punishment or
even dismissal if warnings are ignored.

9. Students are prohibited from going out of the college premises during college hours without the prior permission
of the Principal. They are advised to utilize their leisure time in the College library/common room/canteen. They will
not be allowed to loiter or sit in the veranda.

10. Ragging in any form, inside or outside the campus, is strictly prohibited by law. Any student found indulging in
ragging will be expelled from the College.

11. The College is a No Smoking/ No Tobacco/ No Drugs/ No Alcohol Zone. Students found violating these rules will
be dealt with as per rules of the college.

12. Students should not damage the property of the institution. Cost of any damage will be recovered from the
students as compensation.

13. Students will not be included in any anti-social activities or activities causing hindrance to the academic and
administrative functioning of the College. Those found indulging in such activities will face disciplinary action to the
extent of expulsion from the college.

14. During the teaching hours all areas around the classrooms will be observed as Silent zones. The authority will
deal with students who create any disturbance, as it deem right. Keep silence when the classes are on.

                                                                                                             Page | 11
 15. Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during class and examination hours. Any violation is subject to severe
disciplinary action.

16. No student shall intentionally or recklessly disrupt or impede or attempt to disrupt or impede the activities and
functions of the college, or any part thereof.

17. Irregular attendance, constant negligence of assignments will be severely dealt with. A minimum attendance of
75% is required to appear in the university examinations. In case of absence due to unavoidable circumstances, prior
permission from the appropriate authority must be obtained, and the handbook must be endorsed. In case of
sickness, students will have to produce a Medical Certificate with a guardian's application.

18. Class tests, Unit tests, Assignments, and Terminal/Sessional examinations are obligatory for all students. No one
should absent himself/herself for an examination/test. If a student is absent for a test or examination, a retest or
reexamination will not be given, except on medical/genuine grounds.

19. No candidate shall make use of any unfair means in any examination.

20. Students’ participation and active co-operation in all observation days and other co-curricular activities is must.

Students' responsibilities:
1. Appreciate the institutional goals and objectives and contribute to their realization by participating in relevant
institutional activities
2. Have a clear knowledge of the programs, admission policies, rules, and regulations of the institution.
3. Understand the teaching and learning strategies and evaluation systems of the institution.
4. Follow the time schedules, rules, and regulations of the institution.
5. Undertake regular and intense study of learning materials.

Organization and Management:

Administration: The Governing Body is the apex body duly formed by D.H.E. Assam. The Principal, the Head of the
institution, is the secretary of the G.B.
Committees/Cells/Clubs: For the smooth functioning of the administrative as well as academic activities of the
College, there are a number of committees/cells/clubs:
Statutory Committees: i) Anti-Ragging Cell, ii) Grievance Redressed Cell, iii) Internal Complaint Committee (ICC), iv)
ST/SC/OBC/MOBC Committee, v) Equal Opportunity Committee.
Non-Statutory Committees: i) Academic Committee, ii) Admission Committee, iii) Disciplinary Action Committee, iv)
Career Guidance & Placement Cell, v) Disaster Management Cell, vi) Eco Club, vii) NSS Unit, viii) The Bharat Scouts &
Guides, ix) UBA Committee, x) ELC Unit, xi) Red Ribbon Club, xii) Women Cell, xiii) Yuba Tourism Club, xiv) Alumni
Association.
 Hostel Facility: The College has one Girls’ Hostel with 25 nos. of seats. Admission is purely on merit basis.

 EXAMINATIONS
         The College Examinations are held in accordance with the College Academic Calendar. A student must
appear in all the examinations conducted by the College during an academic year. The College adheres to the rules
and regulations of Gauhati University. As such, a student’s performance is strictly monitored through continuous
assessment in the theory and practical courses. Internal assessment is based on sessional examinations, home
assignments, seminars, projects, group discussions, fieldtrips, class attendance, etc. At the end of each semester, a
final external examination is conducted as per the schedule fixed by the University. A student's final result will be
based on the total marks obtained in both internal and external examinations. Students must secure pass marks in
both internal and external examinations separately.

                                                     Anti-Ragging
     In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (g) of sub-section 1 of section 26 of the UGC Act, 1956, the UGC
hereby makes the regulations, namely: “UGC Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational
Institutions, 2009”. The College has decided to implement the UGC anti-ragging regulations.
What Constitutes Ragging:
Ragging constitutes one or more of the following acts

(a) Any conduct by any student or students whether by words spoken or written or by an act which has the effect of
teasing, treating or handling with rudeness a fresher or any other students.

(b) Indulging in rowdy or undisciplined activities by any student or students which causes or likely to cause
annoyance, hardship, physical or psychological harm or to raise fear or apprehension thereof in any fresher or any
other student.

(c) Asking any student to do any act against his/ her will which has the effect of causing or generating a sense of
shame, or torment or embarrassment so as to adversely affect the physique or psyche of such fresher or any other
student.

                                                                                                               Page | 16
 (d) Any act by a senior student that prevents, disrupts or disturbs the regular academic activity of any other student
or a fresher.

(e) Exploiting the services of a fresher or any other student for completing the academic tasks assigned to an
individual or a group of students.

(f) Any act of financial extortion or forceful expenditure burden on a fresher or any other student by students.

(g) Any act of physical abuse including all variants of it: sexual abuse, homosexual assaults, stripping, forcing obscene
and lewd acts, gestures, causing bodily harm or any other danger to health of person.

 (h) Any act or abuse by spoken words, emails, posts, or public insults, which would also include deriving perverted
pleasure, vicarious or sadistic thrill from actively or passively participating in the discomfiture of fresher or any other
students.

(i) Any acts that affect the mental health and self-confidence of a fresher or any other student, with or without
intent to derive a sadistic pleasure or show off power, authority, or superiority by a student over any fresher or any
other student.

A. Administrative action in the event of ragging:
There is an Anti-Ragging Committee and an anti-ragging squad in the College. The Anti-Ragging Committee shall take
an appropriate action as per the provision under “UGC Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher
Educational Institutions, 2009” in regard to punishing students depending on the nature and gravity of the offense
established by the Anti-Ragging Squad. Following is the Anti-Ragging Committee in our College:
